analogy.name: A document vs a map link
analogy.line: A value type is like a photocopy: change your copy and the original is untouched. A reference type is like a link to one shared document: everyone with the link edits the same file.

csharp-core.caption: Copying a value type copies the data. Copying a reference type copies the address, so both names point at one object.
steps: A photocopy is a value type. Real name: structs and primitives, copied on assignment, so the original never notices your change.
A shared link is a reference type. Real name: classes live on the heap and assignment copies the address, so a change through either name shows through both.

analogy.name: A post office sorting line
analogy.line: A request is like a parcel on a sorting line: the loading door (Kestrel) takes it in, stations check and stamp it (middleware), then the right counter (endpoint) handles it.

aspnet-core.caption: Middleware runs in the order you register it. Auth before routing means a request can be stopped before it ever reaches your code.
steps: The loading door is Kestrel. Real name: the built-in web server that takes the connection, fast and without IIS in front.
The sorting stations are middleware. Real name: logging, auth and routing run in registration order, and any can stop the request.
The counter is the endpoint. Real name: your handler. By the time it runs, auth has passed and the route has matched.
The parcel goes back out the same line. Real name: the response travels through the middleware again, in reverse order.

analogy.name: A translator at a bank
analogy.line: EF Core is like a translator: you speak C# to the clerk, he writes the request in the bank's language (SQL), and he keeps a note of every account he handed back.

efcore.caption: You write LINQ, EF Core writes SQL. The N+1 problem is what happens when the translation runs once per row instead of once.
steps: You speak to the translator in C#. Real name: LINQ, written against objects, not SQL strings.
The translator writes the bank's language. Real name: an expression tree becomes SQL. If it cannot translate something, it throws.
The bank runs the request. Real name: one query, one round trip, unless a lazy load fires once per row, which is N+1.
The translator keeps notes on what was handed back. Real name: the change tracker, so SaveChanges knows exactly what to write.

analogy.name: A warehouse with a fast lane
analogy.line: The CLR is like a warehouse: a packer turns instructions into ready goods when first needed (JIT), new items sit on a near shelf (Gen 0), survivors move back, and oversized crates go straight to a loading bay (LOH).

dotnet-runtime.caption: The CLR compiles once, then collects in generations. Survivors age upward, and big objects skip the queue to the large object heap.
steps: The packer is the JIT. Real name: IL is compiled to machine code on first use, and tiered so hot code gets compiled better.
The shelves are generations. Real name: most objects die young in Gen 0, survivors age into Gen 1 then Gen 2, where collections are rare and costly.
The oversized crate bay is the LOH. Real name: objects over 85,000 bytes skip generations and are collected only with Gen 2.
